reviews.comment: Bluemel is a very sweet lady but she does not have a structured class. The syllabus is nothing like how the class actually is. We had 4 exams, no homework. She does not use canvas so you never really know your grade and she emails slides after the lecture, not an interesting class at all. It is hard because I have no clue what to expect on exams.

Bluemel is pretty soft-spoken, which in a 400-person lecture hall, really really sucks. I couldn't hear her, and I sat in the 4th row. She's super nice, but please try to get another prof. If you do get Bluemel, go to office hours :)
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the most humble and caring professors in chemistry

Honestly a terrible professor, I would not recommend her to anyone. Between her thick accent, terrible microphone, random tangents, and lack of actually teaching.. her class was a nightmare. She very obviously knows what she is talking about, but is awful at teaching it. I had to do a lot of self study and watch YouTube videos just to get through.

She was ok at teaching, but honestly she need to buy a new mic because I can't hear anything from the back of the lecture hall. With her thick accent combined with a bad mic, I basically learned the course by myself at this point. The exam and quiz was not too bad considering I've never been taken chemistry before. Moderately hard A, if put effort

Bluemel is not a good professor. During lectures she spends too long talking about useless information that isn't on the tests or quizzes and then skims over the important information and equations. Expect to learn most of the material from the homework. iClicker attendance and accuracy are part of grade. No curves, very little extra credit

Professor Bluemel was extremely nice and obviously knowledgeable when it came to chemistry. She was always willing to meet outside of class for office hours and had informative lectures. Even if you didn't pay attention during the lectures, just doing the homework would be sufficient enough to get an A. Nice lady overall and very underappreciated.
Dr. Bluemel is a very nice lady, but a lot of what she says gets lost between the large lecture hall and her thick accent. The Dark Souls of Chem 107.

Bluemel's lectures aren't helpful. HOWEVER her Fall 2023 homework, quizzes, and tests were easier than what I've heard from other higher rated professors. Her homework was MUCH shorter than other better rated Chem 107 professors.

If you are confident in your self learning capabilities, I'd suggest you take Bluemel for the easier work and tests.

Professor Bluemel is a nice lady and cares about chemistry. However, she is NOT a good professor. Her lectures are very confusing and she often spends a lot of time talking about things that are not tested over, wasting class time. Sometimes we even got homework that covered material we hadn't learned yet. I wouldn't recommend her to anyone.

The only reason I passed this class was because I had taken AP Chemistry already. Her lectures are confusing and make no sense. She teaches assuming you already understand chemistry. There is not alot of work outside of class but attendance is mandatory until the end of semester. If you are not good at chem or have not taken chem do not take her!!

Great lady, very kind. Does not seem like she knows much about the grading policies, curves, expectations, etc. She only comes in and lectures from slides but is present for office hours. She talks in circles about stuff that doesn't directly apply to material being tested and would explain something and say "its simple". Not great prof, but nice.

She has an extremely thick accent that is very hard to understand and makes lectures difficult to pay attention to. Her lectures also do not go over the material in depth and you are forced to study the textbook which can be very convoluted and overbearing at times. I would not reccomend taking her.
goes off into tangents a lot in class and does not know how to teach material well. homework is graded by what you have by the due date, no late homework is accepted. take anyone else but her.

Not it. She knows what she's talking about but does not know how to present the knowledge in a way the class understands. So in the end, we leave confused. If you haven't taken chem AP beforehand or even if you have, you'll most likely have to self-teach the subject to yourself which isn't ideal considering this is a first-semester freshman class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Bluemel for Chem 107. Her lectures were confusing, and her lecture slides weren't that helpful. Her slides contained a lot of information, but it's mostly jumbled up without a lot of explanation, and half it is irrelevant.. The examples she does give aren't that helpful either. The homework isn't that bad, but it's pretty time consuming.

Professor Bluemel exhibits ineffective lecturing, providing unclear explanations and frequently diverting off-topic. Her limited assistance and unengaging style hinder student understanding and interest. Most of the material had to be taught by Ol' Reliable Organ Chemistry Tutor which proved useful, but fell short of what was required to know.

If I was able to take a different professor, I probably would. No offense to her because she is nice and intelligent, just her teaching is not top notch. Most of the learning I did from the homework and my quiz average was between a "B" and an "A". The material covered in class is boring but mostly pertinent to the quizzes.

She obviously knows a lot about chemistry, but cannot teach it. I feel a little bad because she was nice, but would just read off slides and not even work out the problems at all. Most other professors at least write out the problems and solve examples. I had to do all the learning outside of class.
Awful Professor. Speaks very quietly in a large room, and even when you can hear her, she is terrible at explaining chemistry to those who haven't taken AP Chem (me included).
She clearly knows what she is talking about but does not know how to convey it.

I took this class this past semester and was forced to drop because of the lack of information in her lectures. Really hard to understand in class, rambles on about things unrelated to the topic, and does a bad job and explaining things to students. i talked to her and hired a tutor, neither of which could pull me out of her lack of experience.
The worst lectures I think I have ever received. The only reason I made it through is because of The Organic Chemistry Tutor.

Dr. Bluemel is really nice and loves chem but she is not a good prof. There are no set grade cut offs and your grade depends on how well you did compared to others. Her lectures just feel so random, idk what we were learning. For covid, her exams were open internet, so she made the exams so long with the intent that we could not finish them.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Only grades are from exams. She is very intelligent and tries to make class interesting, but its just a lot of material to take in. Be prepared to listen to/write everything she says because she will test you over something she mentioned 1 or 2 times. She expects deep understanding of chemistry, not simple regurgitation of equations she gives.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I failed her class and unfortunately had to take her again a year later. Grading is not fair and lectures are boring. Be prepare to memorize because that's all you need to do to get high grade. She is quite conservative in teaching and grading. One more thing, she is not really encouraging and that kinda made me upset since I love chemistry. F

Maybe Dr. Blumel is a good chemist and knows a lot about NMR. But she does not want to teach or does not know how to interpret her knowledge which makes the class boring. Also, for those who enjoy chemistry, she does not cover modern inorganic chemistry (coordination chemisty, symmetry, ...). So, the class would not help you in future chem classes
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bluemel clearly knows a lot about inorganic chemistry, but doesn't seem to know the best way to convey the information to her students. Be prepared to write down every word she says and read the textbook, because many points on exams came from topics she spent 5 minutes on in class. Memorization is your friend in this class.
